title: Bot Support Specialist - Global, Remote
why_it_fits: Customer Support match. 2 skills: zendesk, excel. Yes PH eligibility signal
position_overview:
We're looking for a Pharmacy Bot Support Specialist to provide responsive, thoughtful day-to-day support to pharmacies using TJM automation.

You'll work as part of a customer pod alongside Customer Success Managers, Implementation Leads, and technical teams.

This is not an account ownership role. You won't own the customer relationship, customer strategy, or implementation project.

Instead, you'll be one of the first people our pharmacy customers turn to when they have a question, need help, or tell us, 'The bot isn't doing what we expected.' Your job is to figure out what that actually means.

Sometimes the answer will be straightforward. Other times, you'll need to ask questions, understand the pharmacy workflow, gather examples, look at system information, reproduce the behavior, and document what you've learned so our technical teams can investigate efficiently.

You don't need to be an engineer. You do need to be technically curious, comfortable troubleshooting, an excellent communicator, and willing to keep asking questions until you understand what's actually happening.
key_responsibilities:
What You'll Do:
1. Be a Responsive First Point of Support

You'll help manage incoming day-to-day communication from pharmacy customers across our support channels.
- Respond promptly and professionally to customer questions and reported issues.
- Ask thoughtful follow-up questions to understand exactly what the customer is experiencing.
- Gather the information needed to determine whether something is a question, training issue, workflow issue, configuration issue, product issue, or potential defect.
- Help customers resolve issues that can be addressed without engineering involvement.
- Set clear expectations about what happens next when additional investigation is required.
- Keep customers updated rather than leaving them wondering whether anyone is working on their issue.
- Close the loop once an issue has been resolved.

You won't be expected to have every answer. You will be expected to take responsibility for getting the information to the right person and making sure the question doesn't disappear.

2. Investigate Before You Escalate

One of the most important parts of this role is turning a customer-reported problem into something our technical teams can efficiently investigate.
- Ask targeted questions about what happened before, during, and after the reported issue.
- Gather specific examples, timestamps, prescription or workflow context, screenshots, and other appropriate information.
- Understand what the customer expected to happen versus what actually happened.
- Review available system activity, configurations, logs, and other troubleshooting information.
- Attempt to reproduce reported behavior when appropriate.
- Determine whether the issue affects one scenario or a broader workflow.
- Check known issues and available documentation before escalating.
- Document what you've already investigated so another team doesn't have to start from zero.

Your goal is to make sure engineering spends its time solving technical problems rather than trying to figure out what the problem is.

3. Create Excellent Technical Support Tickets

When an issue needs to move to engineering or another technical team, you'll make sure they receive a clear, actionable ticket.
- What is happening - and what should be happening instead?
- Which pharmacy and workflow are affected?
- When did it happen, and is it reproducible?
- What specific examples demonstrate the problem?
- What troubleshooting has already been completed?
- Is there a workaround, and how is this affecting the pharmacy's operation?

A great escalation means the technical team can begin investigating without immediately coming back for basic information.

4. Understand the Pharmacy Behind the Problem

Software support at TJM requires more than understanding software. You need to understand pharmacy.
- Use your knowledge of pharmacy operations and pharmacy management systems to put customer questions into context.
- Learn how each customer's TJM automation fits into its pharmacy operation and use that understanding to troubleshoot more effectively.

5. Communicate Clearly Through Resolution

Great support isn't only about solving the problem. It's also about what the customer experiences while we're solving it.
- Explain technical information in clear, plain language.
- Provide updates while issues are being investigated.
- Avoid making promises before you have the information to make them.
- Let customers know what we need from them and why.
- Communicate internally when an issue may have broader customer impact.
- Bring in the Implementation Lead or CSM when an issue crosses into their area of ownership.
- Help diffuse frustration through responsiveness, empathy, and clear communication.
- Confirm that the customer is actually seeing the expected behavior before considering an issue resolved.

6. Know When to Pull in the Pod

You'll work closely with Customer Success Managers and Implementation Leads, but each role has a different job.
- Customer Success Managers own the strategic customer relationship, overall customer health, and escalations.
- Implementation Leads own the day-to-day execution of implementations, including workflow documentation, implementation requirements, stakeholder coordination, QA, and go-live.
- Pharmacy Bot Support Specialists provide day-to-day product support, investigate reported problems, gather the information needed to troubleshoot them, resolve what they can, and create high-quality escalations when technical assistance is required.

7. Help Us Spot Patterns

Individual support conversations can tell us a lot about our product.
- Issues that appear repeatedly across customers.
- Areas where customers consistently need additional training.
- Workflows that generate frequent questions.
- Product behavior that creates confusion.
- Documentation or support resources we should improve.
- Potential product enhancements.
- Opportunities to prevent future support issues.
qualifications:
What We're Looking For:
- 2+ years of experience working in a pharmacy environment, such as retail, specialty, mail-order, hospital, long-term care, or compounding.
- Hands-on familiarity with pharmacy workflows and pharmacy management systems.
- Technical curiosity and a genuine interest in figuring out how things work.
- A methodical approach to problems and excellent follow-up questions.
- Clear writing and the ability to document details someone else needs to act.
- Patience and professionalism when someone is frustrated.
- Strong attention to detail and the ability to manage multiple customer questions and support issues.
- Comfort working independently in a remote environment, screen sharing, video meetings, and learning new software.
- Understanding of the importance of appropriately handling PHI and other sensitive healthcare information.

Pharmacy Technician Experience Is Highly Desired

Current or previous pharmacy technician experience is highly desired. Registered or certified pharmacy technicians are strongly encouraged to apply.

If you've worked in a pharmacy, you understand that 'the prescription didn't process correctly' could mean a dozen different things, and you know the questions to ask before deciding something is actually wrong with the pharmacy management system.

Pharmacy Management System Experience

Hands-on familiarity with pharmacy management systems is required for this role.

Experience with systems such as PioneerRx, PrimeRx, Rx30, Computer-Rx, FrameworkLTC, QS/1, or similar pharmacy management platforms is particularly valuable.

Nice to Have
- Previous software or technical support experience.
- Experience training pharmacy staff on technology or workflows.
- Experience supporting software implementations.
- Familiarity with Jira, Zendesk, ServiceNow, or similar tools.
- Experience reviewing logs, configurations, or system activity.
- Basic familiarity with Windows, networking, integrations, or software troubleshooting.
- Experience with healthcare technology, workflow automation, or AI-powered technology.
- Experience in specialty, compounding, long-term care, mail-order, or high-volume retail pharmacy.

What You Don't Need

You don't need to know how to code.

You don't need to be an engineer.

You don't need to be a project manager.

You don't need to own a book of business.

You don't need previous experience working with AI.

You don't need to arrive knowing TJM's technology.

You do need to understand pharmacy, enjoy technology, communicate exceptionally well, and be curious enough to keep digging when the first answer doesn't make sense. We'll teach you the rest.

You'll Probably Love This Role If...

Someone saying 'it's broken' immediately makes you want to know exactly what they were doing when it broke.

You're the person in the pharmacy people call over when something weird happens with the computer.

You ask, 'Can you show me?' a lot.

You enjoy figuring out why something happened almost as much as fixing it.

You know that 'it happens all the time' is not quite enough information to troubleshoot a problem.

You can talk comfortably with a pharmacy technician one minute and clearly document the same issue for an engineer the next.

You don't throw an issue over the fence to engineering and consider your job done.

There's something deeply satisfying to you about finally figuring out why the weird thing was happening.

Why TJM Labs

You'll join a fast-growing company working on a very real problem in healthcare. You'll see our automation working inside real pharmacies and taking repetitive work off the shoulders of pharmacists and pharmacy technicians.

For the right person, this can be a path from using pharmacy technology every day to becoming someone who helps shape how that technology works for pharmacies.
